samples.gvd:
module dual_port_RAM #(
    parameter DEPTH = 16,
    parameter WIDTH = 8,
    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = $clog2(DEPTH)
)(
    input wclk,
    input wenc,
    input [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] waddr,
    input [WIDTH-1:0] wdata,
    input rclk,
    input renc,
    input [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] raddr,
    output reg [WIDTH-1:0] rdata
);

    reg [WIDTH-1:0] RAM_MEM [DEPTH-1:0];

    always @(posedge wclk) begin
        if (wenc) begin
            RAM_MEM[waddr] <= wdata;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge rclk) begin
        if (renc) begin
            rdata <= RAM_MEM[raddr];
        end
    end

endmodule
samples.xml_description:
<module id="asyn_fifo">
    <description>Implement an asynchronous FIFO, FIFO bit width and depth can be configured(parameter DEPTH = 16, parameter WIDTH = 8). The asynchronous FIFO structure is divided into several parts. The first part is dual-port RAM, which is used for data storage. Instantiate dual-port RAM as a submodule, The RAM ports are input wclk, input wenc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] waddr, input [WIDTH-1:0] wdata, input rclk, input renc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] raddr, output reg [WIDTH-1:0] rdata. The second part is the data write controller. The third part is the data read controller. The fourth part is the read pointer synchronizer. The read pointer is collected using the two-stage trigger of the write clock and output to the data write controller. The fifth part is the write pointer synchronizer, which uses the two-stage trigger of the read clock to collect the write pointer and output it to the data read controller.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations.</input>
        <input id="wrstn">Write reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="rrstn">Read reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data to be written into the FIFO.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data read from the FIFO.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">8. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the bit-width of data input and output.</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH">16. The DEPTH is the capacity of FIFO, which is also configurable.</parameter>
        <parameter id="ADDR_WIDTH">4. Internal parameter, ADDR_WIDTH is the address width of dual_port_RAM. ADDR_WIDTH = $clog2(DEPTH).</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential id="raddr_bin">The raddr_bin is the binary address of the read pointer. The size of raddr_bin is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The raddr_bin is incremented by 1 if rempty is inactive and rinc is active. The initial value of raddr_bin is 0.</sequential>
        <combinational id="raddr_gray">The raddr_gray is the Gray code of raddr_bin. The raddr_gray is the XOR operation between raddr_bin and the shift-left-1 operation of raddr_bin.</combinational>
        <sequential id="rptr">The rptr is the Gray code address of the read pointer. The size of rptr is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The rptr is set to raddr_gray if rrstn is active. The initial value of rptr is 0.</sequential>
        <sequential id="rptr_buff">The rptr_buff is the buffer of rptr. The size of rptr_buff is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The rptr_buff is set to rptr if rrstn is active. The initial value of rptr_buff is 0.</sequential>
        <sequential id="rptr_syn">The rptr_syn is the synchronized read pointer. The size of rptr_syn is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The rptr_syn is set to rptr_buff if wrstn is active. The initial value of rptr_syn is 0.</sequential>
        <combinational id="ren">The ren is the internal read enable signal. The ren is active if rinc is active and rempty is inactive.</combinational>
        <sequential id="waddr_bin">The waddr_bin is the binary address of the write pointer. The size of waddr_bin is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The waddr_bin is incremented by 1 if wfull is inactive and winc is active. The initial value of waddr_bin is 0.</sequential>
        <combinational id="waddr_gray">The waddr_gray is the Gray code of waddr_bin. The waddr_gray is the XOR operation between waddr_bin and the shift-left-1 operation of waddr_bin.</combinational>
        <sequential id="wptr">The wptr is the Gray code address of the write pointer. The size of wptr is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The wptr is set to waddr_gray if wrstn is active. The initial value of wptr is 0.</sequential>
        <combinational id="wfull">The wfull is the write full signal. The wfull is active if the wptr is equal to the bitwise negation of the 2 most significant bits of the rptr_syn concatenated with the remaining bits of the rptr_syn.</combinational>
        <sequential id="wptr_buff">The wptr_buff is the buffer of wptr. The size of wptr_buff is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The wptr_buff is set to wptr if wrstn is active. The initial value of wptr_buff is 0.</sequential>
        <sequential id="wptr_syn">The wptr_syn is the synchronized write pointer. The size of wptr_syn is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. The wptr_syn is set to wptr_buff if rrstn is active. The initial value of wptr_syn is 0.</sequential>
        <combinational id="wen">The wen is the internal write enable signal. The wen is active if winc is active and wfull is inactive.</combinational>
        <combinational id="rempty">The rempty is the read empty signal. The rempty is active if the rptr is equal to wptr_syn.</combinational>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <description>
            The module implements an asynchronous FIFO using a dual-port RAM module and additional logic for managing read and write pointers.
            Dual-port RAM:
            The module instantiates a dual-port RAM module named "dual_port_RAM" with configurable depth and width.  
            The RAM module has separate clock inputs for write (wclk) and read (rclk) operations.
            The RAM module has separate address inputs for write (waddr) and read (raddr) operations.
            The RAM module has a write enable input (wenc) and a write data input (wdata).
            The RAM module has a read enable input (renc) and a read data output (rdata).
            The RAM module stores data in a two-dimensional array, RAM_MEM, with a size of DEPTH by WIDTH.
            The following logics from the top module <module id> are used to instantiates the <module id>: wclk, wen, waddr, wdata, rclk, ren, raddr, rdata:
            - wclk to wclk of <module id>.
            - wenc to wen of <module id>.
            - waddr to waddr of <module id>.
            - wdata to wdata of <module id>.
            - rclk to rclk of <module id>.
            - renc to ren of <module id>.
            - raddr to raddr of <module id>.
            - rdata to rdata of <module id>.
            Write and Read Pointers:
            The module includes logic to manage write and read pointers for asynchronous operation.
            The write and read pointers are represented by binary registers, waddr_bin and raddr_bin, respectively.
            The waddr_bin and raddr_bin pointers are incremented based on the write and read increment signals (winc and rinc), respectively.
            The write pointer waddr_bin is incremented on the positive edge of the write clock (posedge wclk) and reset to 0 on write reset (~wrstn).
            The read pointer raddr_bin is incremented on the positive edge of the read clock (posedge rclk) and reset to 0 on read reset (~rrstn).
            Gray Code Conversion:
            The write and read pointers are converted to Gray code using XOR operations with right-shifted values.
            The converted write and read pointers are stored in registers wptr and rptr, respectively.
            The Gray code conversion reduces glitches and ensures proper synchronization of the write and read pointers.
            Pointer Buffers:
            The module includes buffer registers (wptr_buff and rptr_buff) to hold the previous values of the write and read pointers.
            The buffer registers are updated on the positive edge of the respective clocks and reset to 0 on the respective resets (~wrstn and ~rrstn).
            The buffer registers are used to synchronize the write and read pointers for determining the full and empty conditions.
